pages.name: A chord over one second
pages.text: Back to the speeding boat, `f(x) = x²` metres after `x` seconds. P sits on its graph at 3 s and 9 m. The chord from P to Q at 4 s climbs `16 − 9 = 7` m in 1 s, a slope of 7 m per s. That is an average over a whole second, and the boat was speeding up all through it, so as the clock passed 3 s it was going slower than 7 m per s. Drag Q to try other chords.

pages.name: Half a second
pages.task: Q is now at 3.5 s, half a second from P. The boat is then at `3.5 × 3.5 = 12.25` m. What is the slope of the chord from P to Q?
pages.why: `Δy = 12.25 − 9 = 3.25` m over `Δx = 3.5 − 3 = 0.5` s, so `Δy ÷ Δx = 3.25 ÷ 0.5 = 6.5` m per s. That is less than 7, because this chord averages over less of the speeding up.

pages.name: Shrink the gap
pages.text: Now shrink the gap between P and Q, Δx, with the slider. Each shorter chord averages over less of the speeding up, so its slope is a better estimate of the rate at 3 s itself. The table fills in 7, 6.5, 6.1 and 6.01 m per s, and in every column the amount above 6 is the gap itself. The chord swings round towards one dashed line through P, the [[tangent]], whose slope is 6. The lens keeps P and Q in view close up.

pages.name: A thousandth of a second
pages.task: Shrink the gap to 0.001 s. Q is at 3.001 s, where `f(3.001) = 9.006001` m. What is the slope of the chord now?
pages.why: `Δy = 9.006001 − 9 = 0.006001` m over `Δx = 0.001` s, so the slope is `0.006001 ÷ 0.001 = 6.001` m per s. The amount above 6 is the gap again, 0.001.

pages.name: Not zero
pages.text: Why not make the gap zero? Then Q sits on P, Δy and Δx are both 0, and 0 ÷ 0 has no answer: any number times 0 is 0, so 0 ÷ 0 could be any number. Come at 3 s from the other side instead. Chords that end at 3 s, from 2 s and from 2.99 s, read 5 and 5.99 m per s. They sit a little below 6, because the boat was slower before 3 s, and they come up towards 6 from below.

pages.name: From 2.9 s
pages.task: Now Q sits before P, at 2.9 s, where `f(2.9) = 8.41` m. What is the slope of the chord from Q to P?
pages.why: Later minus earlier, `Δy = 9 − 8.41 = 0.59` m over `Δx = 3 − 2.9 = 0.1` s, so the slope is `0.59 ÷ 0.1 = 5.9` m per s. The boat was slower just before 3 s, so this chord reads a little below 6.

pages.name: The tangent
pages.text: Both rows settle on 6, so the speed at 3 s is defined as 6 m per s exactly, not 'nearly 6'. You can bring a chord as close to 6 as you like by shrinking the gap. That settled number is the chords' [[limit]], the [[instantaneous rate of change]] at 3 s, and the tangent is the line the chords settle on. Touching the curve once is not what makes it the tangent: an upright line through P meets the curve once too, but it has no slope. Zoom in on P and the curve looks straighter and straighter, until it is hard to tell from the tangent, which is why the tangent's slope is the curve's rate there.

pages.name: At exactly 3 s
pages.task: Chords from P read 6.1, 6.01 and 6.001 m per s. Chords ending at P read 5.9, 5.99 and 5.999. How fast is the boat going at exactly 3 s?
pages.why: Both sides settle on 6, and a chord can be brought as close to 6 as you like by shrinking the gap. So the speed at 3 s, their limit, is 6 m per s exactly. 6.001 m per s is still an average over 0.001 s.

pages.name: δy/δx becomes dy/dx
pages.text: A small change gets a small delta, δ, so a short chord's slope is written δy/δx. Its limiting value as δx shrinks towards zero is written `dy/dx`, read 'dee y by dee x'. At each point it is one symbol for one number. At 3 s, `dy/dx = 6` m per s, in metres per second because `y` is in metres and `x` in seconds.

pages.task: At P, `y` is 9 m and `x` is 3 s. What is `dy/dx` there?
pages.why: `dy/dx` is the limiting value of δy/δx as δx shrinks, the slope of the tangent at P, 6 m per s. Its d's do not cancel, so it is not `y ÷ x = 9 ÷ 3 = 3`. And it is not worked out with a gap of 0, which gives 0 ÷ 0.

pages.task: Back on the boat, P is now at 2 s and 4 m. Chords from P to 3 s, 2.1 s and 2.01 s read 5, 4.1 and 4.01 m per s. What is `dy/dx` at 2 s?
pages.why: The chords settle on 4, so `dy/dx = 4` m per s at 2 s, slower than the 6 m per s at 3 s because the boat is speeding up. 5 m per s is the average over the whole second from 2 s to 3 s, and `4 ÷ 2 = 2` is `y ÷ x`.
